resources.convention: Reduce needless renders. Subscribe to derived state (a boolean such as `isMobile`) instead of a continuous value (the window width). Update state from its previous value with the function form (`setItems(prev => ...)`) so callbacks stay stable and do not depend on state. Declare effect dependencies with primitive values (`user.id`) instead of whole objects. Move heavy computation into a `memo`-wrapped component so it can exit early while loading. Initialise expensive state with a function (`useState(() => ...)`). Compute derived values during render instead of storing another state and syncing it with an effect.

Bundle size. Import directly from the source file rather than from the barrel file of a large library (an icon set, for example), because a barrel can pull in thousands of modules. Load on demand (`React.lazy` and `import()`) for heavy components not needed on first render. Defer third-party libraries that are not needed right away (analytics, tracking) until after the UI has appeared.

Rendering. Use `? :` when the condition can be `0` or `NaN` (`{count && ...}` prints `0`). Hoist static JSX out of the component so it is not recreated on every render. Lists have a stable, unique `key` (not the array index when the list can be reordered). Every piece of data fetched from the server has all three states: loading, empty, error.

Calling APIs. Independent requests run in parallel (`Promise.all`), not in sequence. Do not `await` earlier than where the result is needed. Cancel or ignore the result of an old request when the parameters change (`AbortController`, a cancel flag) so a slow result cannot overwrite a newer one. Use one client layer for API calls instead of scattering `fetch` everywhere.

Data handling. Use a `Set` or `Map` for repeated membership lookups instead of `includes` on an array. Return early once the result is complete. Merge several filters or passes over the same large array into one pass. Sort without mutating the original array (`toSorted` or copy first): sorting state or props in place causes bugs that are hard to see.
